In elderly patients, a reduction in dosage is recommended for those with impaired kidney function, those taking potentially nephrotoxic drugs, and those who are not adequately hydrated. 2. After oral administration, valganciclovir, a prodrug, is converted into ganciclovir, the active drug. As a result, valganciclovir is expected to have reproductive toxicity. 3. There is no data available on the presence of valganciclovir or ganciclovir in human breast milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its impact on milk production. However, animal studies indicate that ganciclovir is excreted in the milk of lactating rats. 4. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) advises HIV-infected mothers not to breastfeed their infants to prevent postnatal transmission of HIV. Nursing mothers should be informed that breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with valganciclovir due to the potential for serious adverse effects in nursing infants and the risk of HIV transmission. 5. Valganciclovir is generally considered acceptable for use during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. 6. When preparing valganciclovir oral solution, pharmacists must wear disposable gloves during reconstitution and when cleaning the outer surfaces of the bottle and cap. 7. To prepare the oral solution, measure 91 mL of purified water in a graduated cylinder. Shake the bottle to loosen the powder, remove the child-resistant cap, and add approximately half the water to the bottle. Shake the closed bottle well for about one minute. Add the remaining water and shake again for one minute. The prepared solution contains 50 mg/mL. 8. Insert the bottle adapter into the neck of the bottle after removing the child-resistant cap. Dispense the patient package insert, which includes dosing instructions, along with two oral dispensers to the patient. 9. Avoid contact with the skin or eyes. If contact occurs, wash the skin thoroughly with soap and water or rinse the eyes with plain water. 10. Take valganciclovir with food to improve its bioavailability. 11. Handle and dispose of valganciclovir according to guidelines for antineoplastic drugs, as ganciclovir, the active metabolite, shares properties with antitumor agents, including carcinogenicity and mutagenicity. 12. Store valganciclovir tablets and undiluted oral solution at 20-25°C (68-77°F), with excursions permitted to 15-30°C (59-86°F). 13. Valganciclovir is an antiviral medication that is converted in the body to its active form, ganciclovir. It is used to prevent cytomegalovirus (CMV) disease in organ transplant recipients and to treat CMV retinitis in individuals with advanced HIV/AIDS. 14. CMV disease can cause serious infections, including CMV retinitis, which may lead to blindness. Valganciclovir works by slowing the growth of the CMV virus but is not a cure for CMV disease. 15. Some patients may experience worsening CMV retinitis despite treatment. 16. Take valganciclovir exactly as prescribed by your doctor, usually 1 to 2 times daily with food. Swallow the tablets whole. If using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before each dose and measure the dose carefully using the provided measuring device. 17. Wash your hands thoroughly after handling valganciclovir. Avoid contact with broken or crushed tablets, the liquid form, or the dust from tablets on your skin, mucous membranes, or eyes. If contact occurs, wash the area thoroughly with soap and water. 18. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition. For children, the dosage is also based on body size. 19. To maintain a constant level of the drug in your body, take valganciclovir at evenly spaced intervals. Do not change your dose or stop taking it without consulting your doctor. 20. Common side effects include diarrhea, upset stomach, dizziness, drowsiness, unsteadiness, or tremors. Serious allergic reactions are rare. 21. Valganciclovir may decrease bone marrow function, leading to low levels of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. This can result in anemia, increased susceptibility to infections, and bleeding problems. Your doctor will monitor your blood tests and adjust your treatment to minimize these risks. 22. Ganciclovir, the active form of valganciclovir, may reduce fertility in both men and women and may harm an unborn baby. It has caused tumors in laboratory animals and should be considered potentially carcinogenic in humans. 23. Women of childbearing age should have a pregnancy test before starting valganciclovir. Effective contraception should be used during treatment and for at least 30 days after stopping the medication. 24. Men with female partners should use effective barrier protection (e.g., latex or polyurethane condoms) during treatment and for at least 90 days after stopping the medication to prevent pregnancy. 25. It is unknown if valganciclovir passes into breast milk. Due to potential risks to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. 26. Valganciclovir may interact with other medications, potentially altering their effects or increasing the risk of serious side effects. Inform your doctor and pharmacist about all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products. 27. Avoid taking ganciclovir instead of valganciclovir without consulting your doctor or pharmacist. 28. If someone overdoses on valganciclovir and experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately. 29. Regular medical and laboratory tests, such as complete blood counts, kidney function tests, and eye exams, should be performed while taking valganciclovir. 30. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. 31. Store valganciclovir tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Store the liquid form in the refrigerator and do not freeze it. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly. 32. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about valganciclovir and your specific health needs.
